English or original-language term acceptable. Rimbaud explored his relationship with Paul Verlaine in two sections of A Season In Hell titled for this word, which are subtitled for the “alchemy of words” and an “infernal bridegroom.”

bonuses.leadin: A glutamine-dependent signaling cascade that initiates this process begins with de-uridylation of P-II and GlnK, culminating in the transcription of nif genes. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this process. An enzyme central to this process uses 16 ATP molecules in tandem with molybdenum-iron or vanadium-iron cofactors to reduce its triply-bonded substrate.

Low nitrogen triggers rhizobia to secrete signaling lipochitooligosaccharides (“lipo-kite-oh-oligo-saccharides”), which are factors named for stimulating and forming these structures. These structures are mutualistic interaction sites between plants and nitrogen-fixing bacteria.
Nodules are affixed to these plant organs, which are responsible for uptake of inorganic nutrients and water from soil.

bonuses.leadin: Over a thousand children have been poisoned by a free school meal program in this country. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this country where protests erupted over lavish monthly housing allowances for members of Parliament. The death of ojek(“OH-jeck”) driver Affan Kurniawan further inflamed protests in this country.

bonuses.leadin: In the prologue to an autobiographical novel titled for a “Report” to this country, an author describes God telling him to “Reach what you cannot!” For 10 points each:
parts: What country is the setting of a novel in which the narrator sleeps in a hut owned by Madame Hortense and tries to re-open a lignite mine?

Nikos Kazantzakis called this figure one of his four “decisive steps” in Report to Greco. Kazantzakis wrote a “Modern Sequel” to an epic about this figure in which he returns to Ithaca after the Trojan War.

bonuses.leadin: These molecules are protonated by water, preventing the formation of a magnesium intermediate. For 10 points each:

bonuses.leadin: This state’s largest body of water, the Quabbin Reservoir, feeds its largest city and means “meeting of the waters” in Nipmuc. For 10 points each:
parts: What state’s place names include Lake Char·gogg·a·gogg·man·chau·gga·gogg·chau·bu·na·gung·a·maugg, as well as the England-inspired Charles River and university-dense city of Cambridge?

This town on the Massachusetts North Shore home to a Singing Beach is also named for an English place, but added a location-based phrase to its name in 1989 to disambiguate from a larger city in nearby New Hampshire.

bonuses.leadin: Alleged parentage by Ixion led to the name of Ixionidae for these creatures. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these Greek mythological creatures. Rhoecus (“REE-kuss”) and Hylaeus, who are killed by Atalanta during their failed attempt to assault her mid-hunt, are examples of these half-horse, half-human creatures.

Ixion fathered the centaurs with the cloud-nymph Nephele while she was disguised as this deity, for whom a sculptor named Rhoecus built a temple in Samos. This Greek goddess turns Galanthis into a weasel for allowing the birth of Alcmene’s (“alk-MEE-nee’s”) son.

The rich man Rhoecus of Cnidus is blinded by one of these animals sent by his hamadryad (“ham-uh-DRY-ad”) lover for brushing it away while gambling. One hero has to sacrifice four bulls and four cows to save some of these animals that are inflicted with disease after Eurydice’s death.

bonuses.leadin: According to this historian, alcohol consumption was only virtuous when done to honor God rather than for personal pleasure. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this historian whose Life of the Fathers consists of 20 hagiographies. This bishop’s Historia Francorum provides much of our knowledge on Early Frankish and Merovingian History.

Gregory of Tours, in his Historia Francorum, wrote of how this person’s army “by the use of magic arts caused various false appearances to arise before their enemies.” He also wrote how Theodoric was killed in battle by this king of the Huns.
Much of Book IV is dedicated to how Clothar I crushed a rebellion of these people. Charlemagne torched their sacred tree, Irminsul, during an invasion when they were led by their king Widukind.

bonuses.leadin: One of this artist’s earliest surviving works shows a view of the deserted Boulevard du Temple (“TOM-pluh”). For 10 points each:
parts: Name this artist and inventor who patented a process of creating images using mercury vapor on an iodine plate.

This photographer of The Kiss of Peace was inspired by seeing the work of Daguerre and his rival Henry Fox Talbot to take up photography. This photographer made many soft-focus portraits of Victorian intellectual figures like Charles Darwin and Alfred, Lord Tennyson.

Julia Margaret Cameron was a photographer associated with this art movement. Dante Gabriel Rossetti founded this art movement, which sought to return to the artistic principles of the early Renaissance.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about changes made to the Kazakh alphabet in the past century, for 10 points each.
parts: Kazakh had first used an Arabic alphabet with added vowels, making it [emphasize]unlike this kind of writing system in which only consonants are represented. Semitic languages like Hebrew and Syriac now use “impure” systems of this kind.
Until a 2017 decree to switch to the Latin alphabet, Kazakh used this script also used by Ukrainian and Russian.

The letter N with tilde unusually represents a velar in the 2021 Kazakh Latin alphabet, whereas in Spanish it represents a voiced consonant that has this place of articulation and manner of articulation. Name both.

bonuses.leadin: In this story, two men who are pinned beneath a tree share a wine flask and imagine what it would be like if they “rode into the market square together.” For 10 points each:
parts: Name this story in which the reconciliation of the feud between the Znaeym (“z’NAY-um”) and von Gradwitz families is cut short by the one-word sentence “Wolves.”
“The Interlopers” is by this pseudonymous British author, whose collection Beasts and Super-Beasts also contains the story “The Open Window.”

In a story by Saki with this title, a bachelor entertains three children on a train by describing a “horribly good” girl being eaten by a wolf. An essay by Walter Benjamin (“BEN-ya-meen”) with this English title examines the works of Nikolai Leskov.

bonuses.leadin: An alternative to operational transformations in collaborative software are data types named for being “[this word]-free.” For 10 points each:
parts: Name this word, which also describes a situation that occurs when attempting to use the “git merge” command on incompatible branches.

Conflict-free replicated data types can be used to implement collaborative text editors with the “strong” form of this two-word property, the requirement that all nodes in a distributed system converge to the same state if no further updates are made.

CRDTs enable collaborative text editors that are “local-first” and avoid using this type of storage. Most collaborative text editors like Google Docs sync to this type of storage, in which data is stored in remote servers accessible via the Internet.

bonuses.leadin: Camilla Townsend traced how this state’s depiction of the Spanish conquest shifted in the 1540s to emphasize peace negotiations instead of their initial resistance. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Nahua state that allied with Hernán Cortés to fight against the Aztecs, their long-time rivals in the Flower Wars. For its help, this state was granted privileged status within New Spain.
In depictions from the Lienzo de Tlaxcala codex, this figure was often drawn larger and more central than Cortés. This Nahua woman translated for the Spanish and secured the Tlaxcala alliance.
According to Bernal Díaz’s history of the conquest, Cortés was addressed as “Malinche” by a ruler of this name. An Aztec king of this name received Cortés in Tenochtitlan and later died in captivity.

bonuses.leadin: This man suggested that improbable theories are more scientifically valuable, since they are more informative and thus more testable. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this thinker who proposed solving the demarcation problem by treating falsifiability as the feature distinguishing scientific theories from pseudoscientific ones in The Logic of Scientific Discovery.

In Conjectures and Refutations, Popper derived a formula for ascribing this property to a theory. This idea’s namesake philosophical problem concerns how to evaluate the degree to which a false proposition is false.

Popper claimed that Hume’s problem of this process, which draws general conclusions from past experiences, was unsolvable because science is instead based on deductive reasoning rather than this kind of reasoning.

bonuses.leadin: According to one New Age movement, this figure flew a fighter jet to Earth from Saturn as part of a diplomatic mission of the “Interplanetary Council.” For 10 points each:
parts: Name this dark-skinned deity whose birth is celebrated in the Janmāshṭamī (“junn-MAHSH-tuh-mee”) festival.

The bhakti(“BUCK-tee”) form of this activity associated with Krishnaism became popular in the West in the 20th century. Buddhists and Jains also perform this practice that often features meditation, breath control, and flexibility.

This founder of Transcendental Meditation and disciple of Guru Dev developed a technique of hopping while cross-legged in meditation called yogic flying, which he proselytized heavily in the West through his spiritual mentorship of popular musicians.

bonuses.leadin: A group of this many Black students in Rock Hill, South Carolina, pioneered the “Jail, No Bail” strategy after being arrested at a sit-in. For 10 points each:
parts: What number also appears in the most common name of a 1972 anti-discrimination provision in education authored primarily by Patsy Mink?
In 1957, Dwight Eisenhower sent federal troops to this southern capital city to escort a group of nine Black students desegregating a high school.

This activist recruited nine Black students from Tougaloo College for a sit-in at a library. This NAACP field secretary was rejected from a school that he later advised another Black student to successfully desegregate.

bonuses.leadin: Kamau Brathwaite depicted the African diaspora in this country in The Arrivants: A New World Trilogy. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this island nation. George Lamming’s autobiographical novels In the Castle of My Skin and The Emigrants depict life growing up in this country and characters traveling from here to England, respectively.
This author drew on her experience working as an au pair in New York City for her novel Lucy. This Antiguan author of Annie John took part of her pen name from another Caribbean country.

Edwidge Danticat (“ed-WEEJ don-tee-KAH”) included autobiographical flashbacks of growing up in Haiti in a novel titled for one of these people. A Fyodor Dostoyevsky novel is titled for three people with this relationship surnamed Karamazov.

bonuses.leadin: Johannes de Garlandia and a text attributed to Anonymous IV are the two main sources for composers from this institution. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this institution home to a medieval school of polyphony where composers like Pérotin (“pay-ro-TAN”) developed organum.

One of the oldest surviving examples of these pieces was written by the ars nova composer Guillaume de Machaut (“ghee-YOHM duh ma-SHOW”) and named for Notre-Dame. These pieces set the Catholic liturgy to music.

This composer was called “optimus organista,” or the master of pure organum, in contrast with discant. Anonymous IV credits this composer with creating the Magnus Liber, which Pérotin revised and added to.

bonuses.leadin: Amiable With Big Teeth, a novel about a group of activists from this neighborhood, remained unpublished until 2009 when it was discovered by a graduate student at Columbia University. For 10 points each:
parts: Claude McKay wrote about black sex workers in the titular poem from his collection titled for this neighborhood’s Shadows. A poem by Langston Hughes titled for this neighborhood asks, “what happens to a dream deferred?”
This poem from Harlem Shadows tells the reader “we’ll face the murderous, cowardly pack” and responds “let it not be like hogs” to this poem’s title statement.

McKay also wrote a novel titled for a city in this country in which the sailor Lafala falls in love with Alima. In a James Baldwin novel set in this country, the title character strangles his boss after a gay love affair with David.

bonuses.leadin: HNH and RuvC are key endonuclease domains in an enzyme that is used in this pathway. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this gene editing pathway originally found in bacteria that often uses an RNA-guided endonuclease to induce edits in a target region of DNA.

This 2-to-6-base-pair DNA sequence downstream of the target DNA sequence must be recognized by the endonuclease for successful DNA binding in CRISPR editing. For the endonuclease SpCas9, this sequence is NGG.
CRISPR can be used to create knockout mutants in this organism that includes the BALB/c albino strain. These rodents smaller than rats are used as common model organisms in labs.

bonuses.leadin: A band performed on top of forklifts that followed behind an animatronic one of these animals in Liverpool to mark its status as 2008’s European Capital of Culture. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these animals exemplified by La Machine’s La Princesse. In 2025, the Tate Modern celebrated its 25th anniversary by installing a large stainless steel sculpture of one of these animals in Turbine Hall.

A spider is depicted in Louise Bourgeois’s Maman, a version of which stands outside a museum of this name in Bilbao. A New York museum of this name displays art around a spiral ramp designed by Frank Lloyd Wright.

The version of Maman at the Guggenheim Bilbao is made of this material. Michelangelo’s Dying Slave inspired an 1877 sculpture in this material that was so lifelike, its artist was accused of casting a live model.

bonuses.leadin: Observation of this process would confirm the existence of elementary Majorana (“ma-yo-RA-na”) fermions. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this type of nuclear decay that emits only two electrons but also violates lepton number.
The nEXO experiment plans to measure neutrinoless double beta decay in liquid xenon-136 via this process, in which ionizing radiation is absorbed by a material and then re-emitted as light.
Experiments observing neutrinoless double beta decay also serve to bound this physical quantity for neutrinos, which is less than one electronvolt, or 1.782 times 10 to the negative 36 kilograms.

bonuses.leadin: Naranjo-style pottery suggests that this city may have conquered the distant site Takalik Abaj (“ah-BAH”). For 10 points each:
parts: Name this city whose Pyramid of the Sun flanks its Avenue of the Dead.

Monument 23 at Takalik Abaj also suggests influence from this civilization, whose conquest of Takalik Abaj predates the Teotihuacan conquest. This civilization, with sites at La Venta and San Lorenzo, is best known for creating colossal heads.
Monument 9 at Takalik Abaj depicts a faded one of these animals staring at the viewer. An ajaw(“ah-HOW”) from Teotihuacan, usually identified with these animals, conquered Tikal.
